liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Easy Wind** (2 reviews): Pigpen starts out fiercely; the band catches up once the jam section kicks in and the studio rocks; Reviewer considers Easy Wind pretty good [6][7]
- **Candyman** (2 reviews): Reviewer hears this as the first Candyman slowed from the earlier double-time folk-country feel into its lasting form; Reviewer's favorite Candyman, praising Garcia's vocal, especially the verse that follows the solo [8][9]
- **Brokedown Palace** (1 other source): Brokedown Palace leads directly into Uncle John's Band [1]

## The recordings

- **gd70-08-30.fm.jupile.12762.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 5 songs; 29 min; rated 4/5 by 12 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound is passable but not great; some passages are muddied and distorted; Reviewer says the audio sounds better than their own video tape of the show; Reviewer says the sound is disappointing for a KQED broadcast, worse than some roadie-made recordings [3][7][10][12][14]
- **gd1970-08-30.sbd.backus.12750.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 5 songs; 30 min; rated 1/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the sound is disappointing for a KQED broadcast, worse than some roadie-made recordings [11]

## Around the show

- Performed live in the studio before a studio audience for a TV program called Calibration [7]
- Show was televised, per the reviewer, as a KQED broadcast [10]
- Show was televised, per the reviewer, as a KQED broadcast [11]
- Reviewer says the band jams harder when Pigpen sings lead [13]
- Calebration was a KQED series with two FM stations, each broadcasting two of four audio channels for quad [14]
- Earlier 1970 Candyman versions are all faster, double-time; this slower arrangement was kept afterward [8]
- Reviewer finds better sound and jamming elsewhere in 1970 on the archive [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-08-30.fm.jupile.12762.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Michael Parrish; transferred by Joe Jupille and Andy Lemieux; source: FM Soundboard [1]
- **gd1970-08-30.sbd.backus.12750.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Dave Backus; source: FM->7inch MR->DAT->CDR->EAC->SHN V.3 [2]
